You are optimizing a batch job scheduler for a university cloud computing project.
The goal is to minimize total makespan (time from first job start to last job finish)
while keeping memcached p95 latency under 1ms at 30K QPS.

Cluster setup:
- node-a-8core: 8 CPUs, ~32GB RAM. Runs memcached + batch jobs.
- node-b-4core: 4 CPUs, ~4GB RAM. Batch jobs only.

Memcached is fixed on node-a with 2 threads, leaving 6 CPUs for batch on that node.
node-b has all 4 CPUs free. Don't overprovision — keep cpu requests (threads * 0.9) within limits.

Jobs to schedule (all 7 must complete, native dataset):
- radix:         ~10s,  scales great (4+ threads ok), barely touches LLC
- barnes:        ~50s,  scales well (2-4 threads), some cache pressure
- blackscholes:  ~60s,  ok scaling (2-4 threads), low interference
- streamcluster: ~150s, scales well (4 threads), low interference, uses a bit of memory
- canneal:       ~180s, barely scales (2 threads is the sweet spot), medium LLC pressure
- vips:          ~200s, ok scaling (2-4 threads), high LLC pressure near memcached
- freqmine:      ~250s, scales ok (2-4 threads), high LLC pressure near memcached

Key things we learned from experiments:
- freqmine and vips both thrash the LLC, which spikes memcached latency if they run on node-a
  with too many threads. Either put them on node-b, or cap at 2 threads on node-a.
- streamcluster is memory-hungry, better kept on node-a (node-b only has ~4GB).
- canneal doesn't benefit from more than 2 threads.
- radix is so fast it barely matters where you put it.

Waves run sequentially — the next wave only starts after all jobs in the current wave finish.
Jobs within a wave run in parallel (as long as there's CPU budget on their node).

Our current best is 378s. The bottleneck was freqmine (167s) and canneal (115s) ending up
in back-to-back sequential waves. Try to overlap the long jobs better.

Scoring:
- slo_factor = max(0, 1 - violation_ratio * 20)  -- any violation ratio above 5% gives 0
- makespan_score = min(1, 378 / makespan_s)       -- faster than 378s scores above 1, capped at 1
- combined = slo_factor * makespan_score

Only modify the get_policy() function. Return valid job names and node names exactly as shown.
Every job must appear exactly once. Don't duplicate or skip any.
